subject: MAP: Throughput & TTFT sprint — test plan, results, and close schedule
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@olivetech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: Throughput & TTFT sprint — initial test plan and deliverables

Hi Jenna —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Attached is MAP_v1.2.pdf with the agreed-upon milestones for the throughput sprint and the evaluation checklist. Quick summary of what we plan to run this week: 

- Goal: validate sustained QPS and per-token economics for the 13B model variant under your production prompt mix.
- Key metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), steady-state tokens/sec, sustained QPS (requests/sec at 95th percentile), and concurrency headroom.
- Targets (pass/fail thresholds): TTFT <= 900ms median, sustained QPS >= 150 req/s for 2k-token average requests, tokens/sec >= 300k at 8 concurrent workers.
- Unit econ snapshot: expected cost/token (op) with moderate batching ~ $0.000012/token; target cost per 1k requests <= $X (see attachment).

Test matrix (high level):
1) Baseline hosted run (no prefix cache)
2) Cached prefix run (30% prefix reuse)
3) Quantized model run (INT8)
4) Dedicated capacity stress (reserve 4 GPUs)

We need: access to a representative sample of 10k prompts, your production traffic window for sustained runs, and procurement contact for committed capacity step. Can you confirm availability for a 2-hour window on Monday/Tuesday for the sustained runs?

Attachments: MAP_v1.2.pdf (mutual action plan with milestones)

Thanks,
Priya

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-02-21T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Throughput & TTFT sprint — initial test plan and deliverables

Hi Jenna —

Great — confirmed for Mon 2/22 09:00–11:00 PT. Answers inline below.

1) TTFT definitions:
   - Cold TTFT: fresh worker process with empty KV/cache — target <= 1.2s (we will measure but not gate the MAP on it).
   - Warm TTFT: steady-state worker with KV primed — target <= 900ms median.
   - We will report both; you said cold-start matters so we’ll include a separate cold-start sweep.

2) 90-day unit-econ projection (assumptions included in cost_summary_v1.xlsx):
   - Baseline (hosted, batching on): $0.000012/token operational cost => 10M tokens/day => $120/day => ~$3,600/mo (~$108k/90d) in op costs.
   - With dedicated capacity (reserved 4x A100-equivalent): amortized infra + infra ops => reduces per-token op cost to $0.000009/token => $90/day => ~$2,700/mo (~$81k/90d).
   - If prefix caching yields 25% token reduction effective, net tokens billed drop to 7.5M/day and costs scale accordingly (see spreadsheet).

Planned tests during the window:
- 09:00–09:30: Baseline throughput ramp (0 -> target concurrency) logging TTFT/first-byte and per-step token throughput.
- 09:30–10:15: Sustained run at target concurrency (8, 16, 32) capturing 95/99 pctl QPS and tokens/sec.
- 10:15–10:45: Quantized model iteration (INT8) for unit-econ delta.
- 10:45–11:00: Wrap + perf regression check against the acceptance thresholds in MAP_v1.2.pdf.

I’ve attached a quick CSV with preliminary sustained QPS runs from our staging cluster to set expectations: sustained_qps_results.csv (note: staging is slightly higher variance than dedicated).

If procurement is ready to review committed capacity terms we can surface a one-pager during the post-run debrief.

See you Monday —
Priya

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-02-22T07:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Throughput & TTFT sprint — instrumentation and test harness notes

Morning team —

Quick tech notes to ensure the results are clean and actionable: 

- Harness: we’ll run our k8s-based runner with deterministic arrival patterns and a separate traffic-replayer for your sampled prompts (to preserve order semantics).
- Telemetry: we will capture TTFT, TTFB, tokens/sec (sampled every 10s), kernel utilization, and GPU memory fragmentation. All metrics pushed to the shared Drive link and Grafana dashboard (read-only).
- Variants: we will test with kernel-optimizer flags A and B (A favors latency, B favors throughput) and include both in the MAP results table.
- Statistical significance: sustained window >= 30 minutes at each concurrency target to minimize variance; we’ll compute 95% CIs for QPS and median TTFT.
- Golden checks: before the sustained run we need explicit sign-off to execute a 15-minute golden test on dedicated capacity (this will incur the reserved instance ramp charge).

Marissa/Karthik — please prep the dedicated pool request; I’ll coordinate the kernel flags and the runner config. Jenna — ack on golden test and PO implications?

-Rishi
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Looking forward to the run tomorrow.

—Jenna
